content: The ounce, abbreviated as oz, originates from the old Italian word onza, now spelled oncia. It is a unit of mass used in various systems, including those that are part of the imperial and United States customary systems. The size of an ounce can vary depending on the system in which it is used. The most commonly used ounces today are the international avoirdupois ounce and the international troy ounce. Definitions Historically, the term ounce has referred to different standards of mass in various parts of the world, at different times, and for different applications. These standards were broadly similar but not identical. Some of these variations are described below. International Avoirdupois Ounce The avoirdupois ounce is the most commonly used ounce today. It is defined as one-sixteenth of an avoirdupois pound, which is equivalent to 28.349523 grams. This unit is widely used in the United States. Although imperial units have been officially abolished in the United Kingdom, the ounce remains a familiar unit, particularly among older generations. International Troy Ounce A troy ounce, abbreviated as t oz, is equal to 480 grains or approximately 31.1034768 grams. There are 12 troy ounces in the now-obsolete troy pound. Today, the troy ounce is exclusively used to measure the mass of precious metals such as gold, platinum, and silver. Apothecaries' Ounce The apothecaries' ounce, now obsolete, was equivalent to the troy ounce and was historically used by apothecaries (now referred to as pharmacists or chemists). This unit is no longer in use in modern pharmaceutical practices. Metric Ounces Some countries have redefined their ounces to align with the metric system. For example, in the Netherlands, the ounce (ons in Dutch) has been redefined as 100 grams, and the avoirdupois pound (pond in Dutch) as 500 grams. These metric values were adopted with the introduction of the metric system and are still informally used, particularly in cooking and grocery contexts. The Dutch metric ounce (1 ons = 100 grams) has also been adopted and taught in Indonesia, where it is formally included in the national dictionary and elementary school textbooks. In East Asia, there is a traditional unit of mass known as the tael, which has varying values. In China, the tael has been standardized to a metric value of 50 grams.
